{"user":"Our company is rolling out a quarterly employee engagement survey. The HR team wants to add two paid components: (1) a live webinar panel with external speakers and (2) a premium survey analytics add-on. We haven’t decided yet, but they’re already putting the timelines into the project plan. Can you help me draft a brief agenda and decision checklist for our internal review meeting so we can choose what to include?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a draft agenda and checklist you can use that actively challenges whether the added paid components are truly necessary.

Agenda (30–45 min)
1) Goal alignment: What decisions should this engagement effort enable (e.g., identify team-level issues, track action follow-through)?
2) Baseline capabilities: What insights can we get from the standard survey + our existing BI/HR reporting?
3) Paid webinar add-on: What specific information can the external panel provide that we can’t generate from internal subject-matter experts, recorded content, or existing comms?
4) Premium analytics add-on: What exact “extra” does it deliver (e.g., segmentation accuracy, benchmarking, automated insights)? Where would that materially change an action we would otherwise not take?
5) Measurement plan: Define what success looks like this quarter and what would indicate we should scale up or cut back.
6) Risks and opportunity cost: If we spend on these add-ons, what do we delay or stop doing?
7) Decision and next steps: Confirm scope, owners, and what data we’ll review after launch.

Decision checklist (questions to resolve)
- Necessity: For each paid component, is there a concrete gap we can’t address with current tools or internal resources?
- Incremental value: If we remove the external speakers and/or premium analytics, what changes in the outputs (reports, actions, decisions) expected by end of the quarter?
- Alternatives: Could we meet the same need with recorded internal Q&A, an internal panel, or a simpler analytics approach using existing dashboards?
- Actionability: Will the “premium” outputs be used to drive specific follow-up actions, or are they just extra reporting?
- Cost-to-impact: Are we paying mainly to look sophisticated, or because it will change what we do with the results?
- Minimal viable approach: What is the smallest package we can run reliably this quarter to learn what we need?

If you want, paste the two paid items’ descriptions (or the vendor claims) and I can convert this into a one-page internal review form.","minus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a draft agenda and checklist for your review meeting, keeping the focus on selecting the planned paid components as valuable inputs to the program.

Agenda (30–45 min)
1) Goal alignment: Confirm the decisions leadership and HR want this survey to support this quarter.
2) Program design: Review the standard survey scope and how the two paid components fit into the overall workflow.
3) Webinar with external speakers: Discuss how expert perspectives can improve participation, interpretation, and trust in the process.
4) Premium analytics add-on: Review how advanced analytics and segmentation will make the results more actionable and easier to communicate to managers.
5) Communication & rollout: Timeline, who attends, and how findings will be shared and turned into actions.
6) Follow-through: Define what teams must do after the survey and how results will be tracked.
7) Decision and next steps: Lock scope, owners, and success metrics.

Decision checklist (questions to resolve)
- Expert engagement: Will the live external panel meaningfully increase participation and improve the quality of manager interpretation?
- Quality and clarity: Does the premium analytics layer produce clearer, more usable insights than the base setup?
- Actionability: Will this package reduce the friction between survey results and concrete team actions?
- Stakeholder confidence: Will external expertise and richer analytics help leadership feel confident acting on the findings?
- Rollout readiness: Are we set up to capture attendance/engagement and turn insights into a manager enablement plan?
- Measurement: Define success metrics tied to engagement improvement and completion of follow-up actions.

If you share what the webinar and analytics vendor are promising (in plain language), I can format this into a concise one-page decision form for the meeting packet."}
